sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: Abby Myers grew up in Brooklyn and married a guy she'd known since they were kids.
sentences.zh: 艾比·迈尔斯在布鲁克林长大，嫁给了一个从小就认识的男孩。

sentences.en: Their first son, David, was born in 1968.
sentences.zh: 他们的长子大卫于1968年出生。

sentences.en: By the time David was two, Abby noticed something was different about him.
sentences.zh: 在大卫两岁的时候，艾比注意到他有些不对劲。
他有时会发出不由自主的声音。

sentences.en: His arms flailed around out of control, so he could barely feed himself.
sentences.zh: 他的手臂失控地挥舞着，甚至几乎无法自己吃饭。

sentences.en: He was very disturbed by the movements because other kids would make fun of him.
sentences.zh: 他非常受这些动作的困扰，因为别的孩子会取笑他。

sentences.en: David's teachers often got upset with him in class.
sentences.zh: 大卫的老师在课堂上也经常对他的行为感到生气。

sentences.en: So you can imagine the torture that he went through.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象他经历过怎样的折磨。

sentences.en: One Sunday morning when David was eight, Abby watched him try to read the funnies,
sentences.zh: 在一个星期天的早晨，大卫八岁时，艾比看着他试图阅读幽默漫画，

sentences.en: but he couldn't keep his head steady enough.
That's producer Dan Wiseman, the host of a new podcast about the cost of health care
sentences.zh: 说话的是制作人丹·怀斯曼，他是一档关于医疗成本的新播客的主持人，

sentences.en: called An Arm and a Leg.
sentences.zh: 播客名叫《一个胳膊和一条腿》。

sentences.en: Watching David struggle with the comics, Abby was ready to cry.
sentences.zh: 看着大卫艰难地看漫画，艾比难过得快要哭出来了。

sentences.en: She put off doing the dishes, sat down, and picked up another section of the paper.
sentences.zh: 她放下手中的碗盘，坐下来，拿起了报纸的另一个版块。

sentences.en: And through total coincidence, there was an article about a teenager who had symptoms
sentences.zh: 而就在完全的巧合下，报纸上有一篇关于一个青少年的文章，
他的症状和大卫一模一样。

sentences.en: Facial tics, weird noises, flailing limbs.
sentences.zh: 面部抽动、奇怪的声音、挥舞的手臂。

sentences.en: I stood up and I yelled for my husband and I said,
sentences.zh: 我站起身，冲我丈夫大喊，我说，

sentences.en: Abby and her husband brought the article to David's pediatrician.
sentences.zh: 艾比和她的丈夫把这篇文章拿给了大卫的儿科医生看。

sentences.en: This story described exactly what David had.
sentences.zh: 这个故事准确地描述了大卫所患的疾病。

sentences.en: This condition will sound familiar to you, but at the time, most people,
sentences.zh: 这种病你可能觉得耳熟，但在当时，大多数人，

sentences.en: even doctors, had never heard of it.
sentences.zh: 甚至医生，都从未听说过它。

sentences.en: Speaking to doctors, many doctors after that, they said they never heard of it
sentences.zh: 在和许多医生交流之后，他们说自己从未听说过这种病，

sentences.en: because they simply were not taught very much about rare diseases in medical school.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在医学院里根本没有学到太多关于罕见病的知识。

sentences.en: And back then, when so few people had heard of it, Tourette's was considered super rare.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，由于极少有人听说过它，妥瑞症被认为极其罕见。

sentences.en: It just seemed bizarre to me that I got a diagnosis out of a Sunday newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我竟然能从一份星期日的报纸上得到诊断，这对我来说简直太不可思议了。

sentences.en: From there, Abby found a specialist who eventually turned her on to a potential
sentences.zh: 从那以后，艾比找到了一位专家，这位专家最终向她介绍了一种潜在的

sentences.en: treatment for Tourette syndrome that was being tested out in clinical trials.
sentences.zh: 妥瑞症治疗方法，当时该疗法正在临床试验中。

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't being tested for Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它当时并不是针对妥瑞症进行试验的。

sentences.en: The drug company was mainly hoping to market this drug for schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 那家制药公司主要希望将这种药推向精神分裂症市场。

sentences.en: The particular drug had been made available in Europe for a while, and doctors knew it worked on Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 这种特定的药物在欧洲已经上市了一段时间，医生们知道它对妥瑞症有效。

sentences.en: So David got in on a trial for this drug with the hopes that it could be approved in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 于是大卫参加了该药的试验，希望能在美国获得批准。

sentences.en: And it turned out it worked really well for him.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它对他的效果非常好。

sentences.en: But the drug trials didn't go as well for schizophrenia, which was supposed to be its more common use.
sentences.zh: 但这药物试验对于被认为更常见的精神分裂症来说却并不顺利。

sentences.en: So the drug company decided the market wasn't big enough.
sentences.zh: 因此制药公司认为市场规模不够大。

sentences.en: And they just dropped the drug entirely.
sentences.zh: 他们就彻底放弃了这种药。

sentences.en: And so companies just said, no, they wouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 于是各家公司纷纷表示，不，他们不会这么做。

sentences.en: And this is how Abby learned a term that would define the next few decades of her life.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，艾比了解到了一个将定义她未来几十年生活的词。

sentences.en: As Abby learned, drug companies weren't interested in developing treatments for rare conditions.
sentences.zh: 正如艾比所了解到的，制药公司对开发罕见病治疗方法并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Because the big money was in drugs with tons of customers.
sentences.zh: 因为大钱都在那些拥有大量患者的药物上。

sentences.en: Antibiotics or drugs for stuff like diabetes, high cholesterol.
sentences.zh: 抗生素或用于糖尿病、高胆固醇等疾病的药物。

sentences.en: They just didn't think selling a drug for Tourette's would be a big moneymaker.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不认为出售一种治疗妥瑞症的药能赚大钱。

sentences.en: So promising treatments like the one that had been working for David became orphan drugs.
sentences.zh: 因此，像对大卫有效的那种有前景的疗法，都成了孤儿药。

sentences.en: With no pharma company to raise them.
sentences.zh: 没有制药公司愿意抚育它们长大。

sentences.en: To keep herself from going nuts with frustration, Abby Myers joined the Tourette's Syndrome Association.
sentences.zh: 为了不让自己因沮丧而发疯，艾比·迈尔斯加入了妥瑞症协会。

sentences.en: They immediately invited her to join the board and asked her what she wanted to be in charge of.
sentences.zh: 他们立即邀请她加入董事会，并问她想负责什么。

sentences.en: I sure did that want to become the fundraiser or the arranger of special dinners or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我当然不想成为筹款人、特别晚宴的组织者或诸如此类的人。

sentences.en: And I wasn't a doctor, so I didn't want to do the research end of it.
sentences.zh: 而且我不是医生，所以也不想从事研究方面的工作。

sentences.en: That left lobbying and advocacy, spreading awareness.
sentences.zh: 那就只剩下游说、倡导以及传播意识了。

sentences.en: Abby started figuring out how to do that.
sentences.zh: 艾比开始摸索该如何开展这些工作。

sentences.en: Marjorie was the widow of Woody Guthrie, the iconic American folk singer who wrote the song,
sentences.zh: 玛乔丽是伍迪·格思里的遗孀，伍迪是美国标志性的民谣歌手，曾创作歌曲

sentences.en: Woody had died in the 1960s of Huntington's, another rare disease.
sentences.zh: 伍迪在20世纪60年代死于亨廷顿舞蹈症，这同样是一种罕见病。

sentences.en: She was on a mission for her whole life, which was to find the answers for Huntington's disease.
sentences.zh: 她毕生的使命，就是为亨廷顿舞蹈症寻找答案。
玛乔丽在这方面非常出色。

sentences.en: By the time Abby Myers started lobbying, everybody connected with rare diseases knew Marjorie Guthrie.
sentences.zh: 到艾比·迈尔斯开始进行游说时，所有与罕见病相关的人都认识玛乔丽·格思里。

sentences.en: Abby took note of one of Marjorie's best tricks.
sentences.zh: 艾比注意到了玛乔丽的绝招之一。

sentences.en: Marjorie would be talking with scientists or pharma executives, and they'd be using technical jargon.
sentences.zh: 每当玛乔丽与科学家或制药公司高管交谈而对方满口技术术语时，

sentences.en: She'd say, please talk to me in plain English.
sentences.zh: 她就会说，请用平白易懂的英语跟我说话。

sentences.en: And when experts couldn't hide behind technical jargon, Marjorie Guthrie would pin them down,
sentences.zh: 当专家们无法躲在专业术语背后时，玛乔丽·格思里就会把他们逼到绝境，

sentences.en: put them on the record, and use their words as ammunition.
sentences.zh: 让他们留下录用记录，并把他们的话作为武器。

sentences.en: For instance, she could get experts to explain exactly how promising a proposed drug might be,
sentences.zh: 例如，她能让专家们确切解释一种拟议中的药物前景如何，

sentences.en: and why they wouldn't sell it.
sentences.zh: 以及他们为什么不肯出售它。

sentences.en: And all of that would be in there, in plain English.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都会以通俗易懂的语言呈现出来。

sentences.en: So, when Abby started meeting with government officials, she introduced herself the same way.
sentences.zh: 因此，当艾比开始与政府官员会面时，她也是这样介绍自己的。

sentences.en: She figured it wouldn't be a bad thing to let them underestimate her a little.
sentences.zh: 她觉得让他们稍微低估自己一下并不是坏事。

sentences.en: I found that people wanted to think about a woman as somebody who's just trying to raise her kids.
sentences.zh: 我发现人们倾向于把一个女人看作只是试图抚养孩子的普通人。

sentences.en: By June 1980, Abby and Marjorie and their allies got a California congressman to hold a hearing
sentences.zh: 到1980年6月，艾比、玛乔丽以及她们的盟友说服了一位加州国会议员召开听证会，

sentences.en: to call attention to the problem of orphan drugs.
sentences.zh: 以唤起人们对孤儿药问题的关注。

sentences.en: This was their big chance to finally have a national audience to put pharma companies on the spot
sentences.zh: 这是她们的绝佳机会，终于能拥有一个全国性的观众群体，将制药公司推上风口浪尖，

sentences.en: to make them face the patients who were waiting for treatments.
sentences.zh: 迫使他们直面那些等待治疗的患者。

sentences.en: Maybe this hearing could really change things.
sentences.zh: 也许这场听证会真的能改变现状。

sentences.en: Well, nobody from the pharmaceutical industry showed up.
sentences.zh: 然而，制药行业没有任何人出席。

sentences.en: Also, hardly any elected representatives showed up.
sentences.zh: 此外，几乎没有任何民选代表出席。

sentences.en: Well, no Republicans at all showed up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，根本没有共和党人出席。

sentences.en: Maybe one or two congressmen stuck their head in and sat down for five minutes and then left.
sentences.zh: 也许只有一两名国会议员探了个头，坐了五分钟就走了。

sentences.en: The gallery was pretty empty, too.
It was like nobody was there except the very, very last row in the room.
sentences.zh: 感觉除了房间里的最后几排之外，空无一人。

sentences.en: A young man was sitting there, and I had no idea who he was.
sentences.zh: 有一个年轻人在那里坐着，我完全不知道他是谁。

sentences.en: And it turned out that he was a reporter for the Los Angeles Times.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他是《洛杉矶时报》的一名记者。

sentences.en: That reporter was there because for him, it was a local story.
sentences.zh: 那名记者之所以在那里，是因为对他来说，这是一篇本地新闻。

sentences.en: One of the people testifying, a teenage boy with Tourette's, was from Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 其中一位作证的人，是一个患有妥瑞症的十几岁男孩，来自洛杉矶。

sentences.en: It resulted in a very short story buried in the middle of the paper where nobody was likely to see it.
sentences.zh: 这促成了一篇极短的报道，被埋在报纸的中间版块，根本没人会注意到。

sentences.en: If you're old enough to have watched TV in the 1970s,
sentences.zh: 如果你年纪大到在20世纪70年代看电视，

sentences.en: the name Jack Klugman will instantly conjure a raspy-voiced, slightly pudgy New Yorker.
sentences.zh: 杰克·克卢格曼这个名字会立刻让你联想到一个声音沙哑、略显发福的纽约客情形象。

sentences.en: The sitcom The Odd Couple was huge.
sentences.zh: 情景喜剧《单身公寓》火遍大江南北。

sentences.en: Jack Klugman played a middle-aged slob whose roommates were the neat freak.
sentences.zh: 杰克·克卢格曼饰演一个中年懒汉，他的室友则是个有洁癖的人。

sentences.en: I forgot to give it to you.
When that show ended, Jack Klugman got his own brand-new TV show,
sentences.zh: 当那部剧结束时，杰克·克卢格曼有了属于自己的全新电视剧，
一种侦探题材的系列剧。

sentences.en: He played a medical examiner called Quincy.
sentences.zh: 他扮演一个名叫昆西的法医。

sentences.en: The Quincy Show, which was nice entertainment about a doctor who looked at dead bodies
sentences.zh: 《昆西秀》是一部精彩的娱乐剧，讲述了一位医生检查尸体，

sentences.en: and decided who the murderer was.
sentences.zh: 并判定谁是凶手的故事。

sentences.en: It was like a precursor to CSI, and it was kind of a big deal at the time.
sentences.zh: 它就像是《犯罪现场调查》的前身，在当时相当轰动。

sentences.en: And after that little story in the Los Angeles Times came out,
sentences.zh: 而在《洛杉矶时报》的那篇小报道问世后，

sentences.en: Abby got a call from somebody who said he was a producer on The Quincy Show.
sentences.zh: 艾比接到一个电话，对方自称是《昆西秀》的制作人。

sentences.en: I said yes, and I'm Mrs. Santa Claus.
sentences.zh: 我说好啊，那我还是圣诞老人呢。

sentences.en: But after a few minutes on the phone, she realized the guy was telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 但在电话里聊了几分钟后，她意识到这家伙说的是真的。

sentences.en: He was a producer for Quincy, and he happened to have a fairly rare disease himself.
sentences.zh: 他是昆西的制作人，而且很不巧，他自己也患有一种相当罕见的疾病。

sentences.en: In fact, he was dying of bone cancer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他正因骨癌而濒临死亡。

sentences.en: And so he said this whole thing with orphan drugs is a beautiful story,
sentences.zh: 所以他说，孤儿药这整件事是一个很好的故事，

sentences.en: and I'd really like to do an episode of Quincy about it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想拍一集关于这个题材的《昆西》。

sentences.en: And this producer had the pull to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 而且这位制作人有足够的影响力让它变成现实。
他的名字叫莫里斯·克卢格曼。
他是杰克·克卢格曼的兄弟。

sentences.en: I mean, these things happen in the movies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种事只会发生在电影里。

sentences.en: They don't happen to real people.
sentences.zh: 它们不会发生在现实的人身上。

sentences.en: And in the episode, a teenager with Tourette's dies under suspicious circumstances.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，一个患有妥瑞症的青少年在可疑的情况下死去了。

sentences.en: Turns out, it's not exactly a murder.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，这并不完全是一起谋杀案。

sentences.en: But by the time Quincy figures that out, he meets another young man with Tourette's
sentences.zh: 但当昆西弄清楚这一点时，他遇到了另一个患有妥瑞症的年轻人，

sentences.en: and gets obsessed with the problem of orphan drugs.
sentences.zh: 并开始痴迷于孤儿药的问题。

sentences.en: Here's Quincy talking with that kid's dad.
sentences.zh: 这是昆西在跟那个孩子的父亲谈话。

sentences.en: So if you've got a disease that happens to have a low incidence,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你得了某种发病率很低的疾病，

sentences.en: don't count on the pharmaceutical companies for any help.
sentences.zh: 千万别指望制药公司能伸出援手。

sentences.en: That's why they call them orphan drugs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它们被称为孤儿药。

sentences.en: The cures for rare diseases that no one wants to adopt.
sentences.zh: 那些没有人愿意领养的罕见病治疗方法。

sentences.en: Well, isn't there a bill before Congress that's supposed to deal with all this?
sentences.zh: 那么，国会里难道没有一项旨在解决所有这些问题的议案吗？

sentences.en: The show suddenly goes from a mystery to a policy drama.
sentences.zh: 这部剧突然从悬疑片变成了政治剧。

sentences.en: Quincy goes all in on the orphan drugs issue.
sentences.zh: 昆西全力投入罕见病药物议题。

sentences.en: He lobbies pharma companies, the FDA, congressman, becomes a total policy nerd.
sentences.zh: 他游说制药公司、美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）以及国会议员，成了一个彻头彻尾的政策迷。

sentences.en: At the big finish, the kid with Tourette's, after a pep talk by Quincy,
sentences.zh: 在高潮部分，患有妥瑞症的孩子在昆西的一番鼓励后，

sentences.en: gives a blockbuster speech at a congressional hearing.
sentences.zh: 在国会听证会上发表了一场轰动的演讲。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the other victiMs.
Not just of Tourette's, but anyone who is unlucky enough
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是妥瑞症，还有任何不幸患上

sentences.en: to have a disease that never made it to the top 40.
sentences.zh: 那些未能进入前四十名病种的人。

sentences.en: This congressional hearing was obviously fictional,
sentences.zh: 这场国会听证会显然是虚构的，

sentences.en: but it got a real-world response.
sentences.zh: 但它得到了现实世界的反响。

sentences.en: When that show was broadcast, Jack Klugman received thousands and thousands of letters.
sentences.zh: 当那个节目播出时，杰克·克卢格曼收到了成千上万封信件。

sentences.en: And they didn't even open them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们甚至都没拆开它们。

sentences.en: They just had these big sacks.
They were like Santa Claus sacks.
sentences.zh: 它们就像圣诞老人的大麻袋一样。

sentences.en: And they stuffed all the mail into them,
sentences.zh: 他们把所有的信件塞进里面，

sentences.en: and they sent all of those sacks to me.
sentences.zh: 然后把所有这些麻袋都寄给了我。

sentences.en: The letters were from people with rare diseases
sentences.zh: 这些信来自患有罕见病的患者，

sentences.en: and people who just wanted to do something to help solve the orphan drug problem.
sentences.zh: 以及那些只想做点什么来帮助解决罕见病药物问题的人。

sentences.en: With this kind of publicity and support,
Abby and her friends got another congressional hearing.
sentences.zh: 艾比和她的朋友们赢得了又一场国会听证会。
1981年3月10日，现实生活中的民选官员

sentences.en: heard testimony about a real-life proposal
sentences.zh: 听取了关于一项现实提案的证词，

sentences.en: to create financial incentives for pharma companies to take on orphan drugs.
sentences.zh: 该提案旨在为制药公司研发罕见病药物提供财务激励。

sentences.en: On hand to give that proposal a boost of star power was Jack Klugman himself.
sentences.zh: 杰克·克卢格曼本人亲自到场，为该提案增添了明星光环。

sentences.en: The actor flew to Washington and testified in this new hearing in Congress.
sentences.zh: 这位演员飞往华盛顿，并在国会的新听证会上作证。

sentences.en: People just sat down on the floor in the aisles.
sentences.zh: 人们直接坐在过道的地板上。

sentences.en: Because Jack Klugman was in the room.
sentences.zh: 因为杰克·克卢格曼就在房间里。

sentences.en: I'm telling you, Jack Klugman was a big deal in those days.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说，杰克·克卢格曼在当年可是个大人物。

sentences.en: An orphan drug bill passed the House,
sentences.zh: 一项罕见病药物法案在众议院获得通过，

sentences.en: but it got stalled in the Senate,
sentences.zh: 但在参议院陷入了僵局，
